A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IMP-Loss/DIMP-Loss study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-I are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments in Section 5, measured runtimes in Appendix E, and noisy-data experiments and checker analyses in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds SunGen comparisons and an out-of-domain contamination condition in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1-2 and the IMP-Loss/DIMP-Loss objectives retain the same quality checkers, fixed or dynamic diversity checkers, weighting functions, and training procedures. The added experiments do not modify the proposed methods.

E1.justification: Financial, Tweet Irony, and MRPC remain the principal tasks. Appendix G adds Tweet Sentiment Extraction examples as unrelated training inputs for the Financial noise experiment, extending coverage to out-of-domain contamination without introducing a separate prediction task.

E2.justification: v2 adds SunGen to the synthetic-data and large-real-world comparisons for all three tasks in Table 1 and to the runtime comparison in Table 3/Figure 3. Figure 2 also adds a CE-Loss reference comparator. Existing comparators are retained; UniGen and FuseGen are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix G.1 extends the Financial noise construction by randomly selecting 452 unrelated sentiment examples, alongside the retained label-swap and duplication conditions. Appendix E specifies one inner-loop epoch for the newly evaluated SunGen baseline. Existing task splits, metrics, model configurations, and hyperparameter ranges remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing robustness analysis now tests unrelated-input contamination and examines its checker scores and weights in Figures 4, 6, and 7. Appendix E extends the efficiency analysis to SunGen. The checker-size, checker-data-size, and diversity-checker ablations are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four random seeds, report the best-accuracy run in tables, and show minimum, maximum, and average training dynamics. Figure 1 is unchanged, and no new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds SunGen scores, and Table 3 adds its 2680-second runtime; existing entries in these tables remain unchanged. Under the revised Financial noise conditions, Table 4 replaces IMP-Loss accuracy/F1 of 81.85/78.93 with 81.6/78.24 and DIMP-Loss 82.51/80.22 with 82.59/80.28, also updating CE-Loss and Focal-Loss. Figures 4, 6, and 7 report revised checker results. These replacements are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The convergence argument, Bayes-rule derivation, and lower-bound proof retain their mathematical substance. Appendix C's expanded Equation 21 explicitly writes the likelihood product already described under the i.i.d. assumption in v1; entropy and dataset notation are clarified without introducing new assumptions or results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: quality/diversity weighting improves synthetic-data training with little real data, and DIMP-Loss offers computational efficiency. Added comparisons support these existing contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation of unrelated inputs as diverse but low-quality and emphasizes computational efficiency when SunGen is competitive. Some new interpretation conflicts with the evidence: Appendix G.3 says original-data diversity-checker scores are lower than unrelated-input scores, whereas Figure 6 shows the opposite ordering.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct code-repository link on page 1, identifies use of SunGen's official code, and specifies its runtime experiment's inner-loop setting. Appendix G documents the new contamination source and sample count. Existing training details, hardware information, prompts, and supplementary code/data statements remain.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds focused discussion of synthetic-data text classification, including SunGen, Meng et al. (2022; 2023), UniGen, and FuseGen. It distinguishes computational costs and proposes compatibility with UniGen/FuseGen. This extends the existing positioning around importance weighting, filtering, and meta-learning without replacing it.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and notation edits, reorders and expands related-work paragraphs, and updates affiliations and publication headers while adding acknowledgments. The main narrative, section sequence, and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 gain SunGen rows; Figure 2 gains a CE-Loss line; Figure 3 gains a SunGen bar and expanded vertical scale. Figures 4, 6, and 7 add unrelated-input bars and legends. Appendix displays shift position, but the overall layout and visualization styles are retained.

improvement.justification: The SunGen accuracy/runtime comparisons and out-of-domain contamination test provide useful additional scrutiny, while expanded related work and code-access information improve context and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by inaccurate new discussion: SunGen's synthetic Tweet Irony accuracy is 78.96%, above DIMP-Loss's 78.44%, despite the claim that it remains below the proposed methods; Appendix G.3 also reverses Figure 6's original-versus-unrelated score ordering. The core methods and principal retained results are unchanged.
